html:
The Battle of Pichincha was fought on 24 May 1822 on the slopes of the volcano Pichincha above Quito. A patriot army under Antonio José de Sucre defeated the Spanish and freed what is now Ecuador.

Simón Bolívar had sent Sucre south by sea to Guayaquil, which had declared independence in 1820. Sucre's army, with troops from Colombia, Peru and Argentina, marched up into the highlands and climbed the volcano by night to outflank the Spanish. A teenage officer, Abdón Calderón, became a national hero for fighting on though wounded.

Quito surrendered the next day. The region joined Gran Colombia, and Bolívar and San Martín met in Guayaquil in July. Ecuador left Gran Colombia in 1830. Pichincha opened the road for the final campaigns in Peru and Bolivia that ended Spanish rule in Ecuador's neighbours.
sum: The Battle of Pichincha was fought on 24 May 1822 on the slopes of the volcano Pichincha above Quito. A patriot army under Antonio José de Sucre defeated the Spanish and freed what is now Ecuador.
